changes.current_line: Built for developers: launch payments fast with our APIs, docs and sandbox.
changes.change: For engineer-led buyers: lead with proof an engineer can build themselves. "Build a working payment flow over a weekend with our docs and sandbox." Pair it with a starter flow and sandbox guide that mirrors a real two-sided payment (onboard a worker, pay them out) so the engineer's own prototype is what the team shows at standup.
changes.why: The deal moved from bake-off to committed after a customer engineer built a working sitter payment flow over a weekend with the docs and sandbox, and our own claim was not what tipped it.

changes.current_line: Onboard, verify and pay out to sellers worldwide, in their local currency.
changes.change: For buyers who run a service app and don't call it a marketplace: "Sitter pay, paid by Friday, in local currency, with identity checks built in. Payments shouldn't be a team." Avoid "marketplace" and "payouts" in headlines for this audience; use "the app" and "sitter pay" style wording (worker pay in the buyer's own terms).
changes.why: The onboarding, identity-check and local-currency payout content got a reaction, but the customer says "paid by Friday," "sitter pay" and "the app" rather than our "marketplace" and "payouts."

changes.current_line: Financial infrastructure to grow globally, in every currency.
changes.change: For engineering-led buyers carrying a homegrown payments system: open with relief from the burden, not global growth. "Payments shouldn't be a team." Follow with: stop having engineers keep payments working so the faster-pay roadmap item can ship, and local pay for new countries comes along with it.
changes.why: The pain was two engineers kept busy on payments and a faster-pay roadmap item pushed three quarters in a row, with expansion to Canada and the UK as the opening rather than the problem.

changes.current_line: Customers see an average uplift in authorization rates with Authorization Boost and Adaptive Acceptance.
changes.change: Stop leading with authorization-rate uplift for low-ticket businesses. Use it only if the buyer raises acceptance first.
changes.why: The acceptance-rate slide drew silence and the customer said "our average booking is 38 dollars, I'm not losing sleep over auth rates."
